messages.content: Write the product page copy for a team chat application, aimed at engineering managers who are choosing between tools. Around 250 words.

Here's the copy. Product name and the concrete numbers are placeholders — swap in your real ones, since the whole approach depends on the specifics being true.

---

# Cadence — team chat for people who have to ship

Your team already has a chat tool. The real question is what it's costing you.

Most chat apps are built for the person typing. Cadence is built for the twelve people who read that thread three days later, when something is on fire and nobody remembers who decided what.

**Threads that don't rot.** Every thread gets a permanent URL and a resolved/unresolved state. Search returns threads, not a firehose of individual messages. Six months of incident context, one query.

**Notifications you can actually tune.** Per-channel, per-thread, per-hour. Set a channel to digest-only and it stays digest-only — no "someone mentioned you" override, no quiet re-enabling after an update ships.

**On-call is first-class.** Point Cadence at PagerDuty or Opsgenie and it knows who's on rotation. `/page` reaches the person holding the pager, not whoever's name someone half-remembers.

**Export is a right, not a plan tier.** Full JSON of every message, file, and thread. Every plan, day one. If you leave, you leave with your data.

What we don't do: video calls, whiteboards, a document editor, a marketplace of 400 half-maintained integrations. Those are somebody else's product, and they're better at them than we'd be.

$6 per person per month. No seat minimum, no annual lock-in, no "contact sales" tier hiding the actual number.

Free for 30 days, with SSO and SCIM turned on. Evaluating an enterprise tool without SSO isn't an evaluation.
Rewrite the text above. Keep the same length and the same purpose. Return only the rewritten text.

output:
# Cadence — chat for teams that ship

You've already got a chat tool. The question is what it's costing you.

Most chat apps are designed around the person typing. Cadence is designed around the twelve people who open that thread on a Thursday three days later, mid-incident, trying to work out who decided what and why.

**Threads that survive.** Each thread has a permanent URL and a resolved/unresolved state. Search hits threads, not ten thousand loose messages. Half a year of incident history, one query.

**Notification settings that stick.** Per channel, per thread, per hour. Set a channel to digest-only and it stays digest-only. No mention override sneaking through, no quiet reset the next time we ship.

**On-call built in, not bolted on.** Connect PagerDuty or Opsgenie and Cadence knows who's carrying the pager. `/page` reaches that person — not whoever's name someone half-remembers from the last rotation.

**Export isn't a plan tier.** Full JSON. Every message, file, and thread, on every plan, from day one. Leave whenever you want and take your data with you.

Things we don't build: video calls, whiteboards, a doc editor, a directory of 400 half-maintained integrations. Other companies do those better than we would.

$6 per person per month. No seat minimum. No annual lock-in, and no "contact sales" tier concealing the real number.

Thirty days free, with SSO and SCIM switched on from the start. An enterprise evaluation without SSO isn't an evaluation.
